title: Smart-seq2
scope: Picelli 2013 Smart-seq2 implementation, extracted at the level of the assigned Illumina schematic and its two Smart-seq2 poster rows. The 2014 protocol is a later clarifying source and is not treated as an identical complete experimental implementation. The neighboring Smart-seq/NanoCAGE/CAGEscan, DP-Seq and snRNA-seq rows are outside this target.

properties.name: biological_representation
properties.definition: Relationship between the physical DNA insert and the original RNA target; full-length cDNA coverage is a design goal, not an assertion that each final fragment is full length.
properties.value: cDNA inserts represent expressed polyadenylated RNA through copying and amplification. Fragmented library inserts need not span an entire original transcript.

evidence.quote: The current limitations are the lack of strand specificity and the inability to detect nonpolyadenylated (polyA(-)) RNA.

properties.name: representation_limits
properties.definition: Supported limitations on interpreting RNA representation from this DNA library; does not assert perfect recovery or molecule counts.
properties.value: The library is not strand-specific. Oligo(dT) priming targets polyadenylated RNA, with non-polyadenylated RNA outside the intended profiling scope; transcript length and abundance affect representation. This is not a claim of perfect priming specificity.

operations.label: First-strand cDNA synthesis with MMLV reverse transcriptase
operations.description: The adapter-bearing oligo(dT) primer primes the poly(A)-tailed RNA. Reverse transcription creates a complementary first-strand cDNA; the depicted product includes the RNA/cDNA hybrid, the primer-derived adapter and a short terminal CCC extension on cDNA.
operations.mechanism: MMLV reverse transcriptase is the named catalyst, rather than a material consumed as template. Oligo(dT) priming relates the cDNA to poly(A) RNA. The CCC symbol summarizes the short untemplated cDNA 3′ extension; it does not specify that every molecule receives exactly three C residues.
operations.information_effect: RNA sequence is represented by complementary DNA. Poly(A)-dependent priming restricts which transcripts are represented; no RNA-fragmentation operation is specified by the source label mRNA fragment.

operations.label: Template switching and first-strand cDNA extension
operations.description: The G-bearing end of the TSO pairs with the C-rich cDNA extension, allowing reverse transcriptase to extend first-strand cDNA using the oligonucleotide as the next template. This is the cDNA synthesis block following first-strand synthesis, not a separately depicted second-strand synthesis step.
operations.mechanism: The GGG/CCC pairing in the figure connects the TSO to the C-rich cDNA end. Generic template-switching chemistry is clarified by Tang et al. [b00004]; the specific 3′ LNA-bearing TSO is identified by the Smart-seq2 diagram and catalogue description. The LNA is a modification of the TSO reagent, not a claim that the synthesized cDNA inherits LNA chemistry.
operations.information_effect: A universal oligonucleotide-derived sequence is appended to the RNA-derived cDNA. This enables subsequent amplification while retaining the copied RNA sequence. The 2013 abstract supports improved template switching but does not independently verify the detailed oligo chemistry.

operations.label: cDNA preamplification by PCR
operations.description: PCR amplifies the template-switched cDNA into the double-stranded cDNA preparation used for tagmentation. This is the PCR before library fragmentation, distinct from the later enrichment PCR.
operations.mechanism: PCR acts through the universal primer/TSO-derived amplification interface. The figure retains this as a single PCR block and supplies no separate second-strand or intermediate-purification route.
operations.information_effect: Amplification increases material representing the source RNA sequences. Amplification and transcript-length biases mean product abundance is not a guaranteed one-to-one count of original RNA molecules.

operations.label: Gap repair, enrichment PCR and library purification
operations.description: The depicted composite block processes tagmented fragments into an enriched, purified adapter-bearing cDNA library with the shown Index 2/P5 and Index 1/P7 terminal regions. Its internal interfaces are not separately drawn.
operations.mechanism: Gap repair and enrichment PCR are named, followed by PCR purification in the same source block. The indexed P5/P7-containing endpoint is shown; the drawing does not allocate individual adapter segments to separate unshown reaction steps.
operations.information_effect: If sequenced, the RNA-derived DNA inserts can support transcript detection and expression profiling for the originating single-cell preparation, subject to representation and amplification biases. Index 1 and Index 2 are depicted library index segments; the figure supplies no cell-barcode or UMI scheme. Sequencing and data processing are outside the depicted endpoint.
